13.12.2023 The petitioners are successors-in-interest of Ashok Kumar Gupta who was owning and possessing land in khasra no. 107/25 min situated in village Chak Shahzada, tehsil and district Kathua and upon his death mutation of inheritance no. 193 came to be attested as is borne out from khasra girdawari of 2022.
In the khasra girdawari of 2022, there is a mention of the petitioners being in cultivating possession of land in khasra no. 107/25 min.

Learned counsel for the petitioners submits that their father- Ashok Kumar Gupta during his lifetime was not aware as to whether any land acquisition exercise had been undertaken resulting in passing of a final award dated 23.05.2011 whereby some portion of a land out of khasra no. 107/25 min owned by their father had come under purported land acquisition exercise for the purpose of widening of national highway

as such the petitioners are impugning the acquisition exercise with the plea that acquisition needs to be taken up afresh under Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013.

sentences.text: Learned counsel for the petitioners further submits that their predecessor-in-interest-Ashok Kumar Gupta never ever came to receive single penny of compensation payable under the said award as he was not aware of any such award having come into existence thereby acquiring the portion of land out of khasra no. 107/25 min.
Prima facie case is made out.
Petitioner to furnish registered postal covers for the service of the respondents within one week whereupon the Registrar Judicial, Jammu to issue notice to the respondents.
